records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253 — The update fallback checks externalId === externalCalendarId only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so updates without a stored external calendar ID fail to use the destination calendar
records.rationale: The diff changes the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` (also repeated in deleteEvent). This fallback branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, in which case `find` compares each calendar's externalId against a null/undefined value and never matches, so the fallback always yields undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId — a regression introduced by this diff in both updateEvent and deleteEvent paths.

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:312 — The deletion fallback uses the same inverted externalCalendarId condition, allowing deletion to target the primary calendar incorrectly or leave the actual event undeleted
records.rationale: The diff changes deleteEvent's fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` inside the branch where `externalCalendarId` is already falsy — so the find can essentially never match, making the fallback always undefined (previously it returned `destinationCalendar?.externalId`). Same inverted condition exists in updateEvent. This can cause deletion to miss the intended calendar. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff hunk.

records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:550 — The merge deletion path uses .find(), so only one old host calendar event is removed and other hosts retain orphaned events when multiple calendar references exist
records.rationale: The diff converts calendar references into arrays (filter for multiple references), but the old-event deletion on merge still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))`, so with multiple destination calendars only one old host's event is deleted, leaving orphaned events on other hosts. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: the surrounding code was updated to iterate over all references while the delete path was left using a single `.find()`.
